The ahardin is a musical bow used by the southern Tuareg. Its body is a curved branch, bound with rope twisted from rawhide or acacia bark; to play, an upturned gourd is set on the ground at the bend of the bow as a resonator and the player presses it steady with the knee. The left-hand fingers decide the melody, and the thumb and index finger of the right pinch the string into vibration in a fixed motion. It is now mostly seen as an instrument for a girls' game. Its feminine form, Tahardant, also names a plucked instrument, current in the Niger Bend, played by the Tuareg court craftsmen and by Songhai griots.
阿哈迪恩琴（Ahardin）的聆聽場合主要見於南部圖阿雷格人的音樂弓傳統。來源指: The listening settings for the ahardin are mainly the musical-bow tradition of the southern Tuareg. The source notes that the instrument is now regarded mainly as a girls' game. The related tahardant appears in the Niger Bend, played by Tuareg court craftsmen and Songhai griots. So the sounds to listen for are the playing in the girls' game and the plucked-instrument settings of the craftsmen and griots in those regions.
